$comment: The v4 slice as end-to-end tests, in priority order. A building session changes ONLY the `passes` field, and sets it true only after `test` passes locally and in CI. Never delete, reword or reorder a feature to make it pass; a feature that turns out wrong gets a new feature plus a note in progress.md. `blockedBy` names what must happen before work starts. See docs/development/workflow.md.

features.description: One schema generates the TS and Go contracts, and every fixture validates in both
steps: make gen twice leaves the tree clean
check-fixtures passes all fixtures with ajv
the Go round-trip test passes and rejects every invalid-required fixture
a schema edit without make gen fails check-gen

features.description: make e2e boots wrangler dev on a free port, waits for /healthz, runs the named e2e tests and prints E2E_MS
steps: make e2e starts the Worker with --persist-to a temp dir
GET /healthz returns 200 within 10 s
a failing step names itself and prints the last 20 events
the run ends with E2E_MS=<n> STEPS=<k>/<k>
features.test: make e2e-a (steps 1 to 3: go test ./e2e -run TestF02; step 4: the closing-line assertion in the Makefile target)

features.description: A test user creates a pod and receives hello over the pod WebSocket
steps: POST /__test/session mints a user and returns a jmu_ token (local and preview builds only)
POST /v1/pods with that token creates a pod and returns its id
GET /v1/pods/:pod/ws with the token upgrades and the first frame is hello with headSeq 0 and the user as owner

features.description: Human messages fan out live, and a reconnecting client resumes from sinceSeq with no gaps
steps: two members subscribe; one sends message.post
both receive message.created with the same seq
the second client disconnects, three more posts happen, it reconnects with subscribe{sinceSeq}
it receives exactly the three missed events, in order
the same holds after the Durable Object hibernates

features.description: Invites add members; used, expired and non-member cases are refused
steps: the owner creates an invite and a second user accepts it
the second user's hello lists them as a member
accepting the same single-use invite again returns 410
accepting an expired invite returns 410 and adds no member
a non-member creating an invite gets 403

features.description: A member creates a task assigned to an agent and every member sees task.created
steps: a registered agent exists in the pod
a member sends task.create with the agent as assignee
all subscribers receive task.created with status open and the assignee set

features.description: Only addressed changes wake an agent, wakes coalesce, and unacked wakes are re-sent
steps: an ambient human message produces no run.wake
assigning three tasks to the agent in a row produces one pending wake, delivered once
a wake not acked within 60 s is re-sent on the next heartbeat (clock is test-controlled)
run.wake goes only to the computer that hosts the agent

features.description: The daemon registers its computer and an agent, and the pod shows the agent online
steps: jellymoon daemon start --foreground registers the computer and stores jmc_ at mode 0600
jellymoon agent add fake registers an agent in the pod
members receive presence.changed online for the agent within 5 s
killing the daemon produces presence.changed offline within 45 s

features.description: On run.wake the daemon claims a run and starts the agent with a run token and the pod MCP server
steps: the daemon receives run.wake and calls POST /v1/runs
the response carries runId, a jmr_ token, a brief and the MCP URL
the fake ACP agent starts with the MCP server passed in session/new
jm_whoami over MCP returns the agent, pod and run
the agent's argv and env contain jmr_ and never jmc_

features.description: jm_task_claim is exclusive, and its lease lives as long as its run
steps: two runs claim the same task concurrently; exactly one wins
the loser gets already_claimed naming the holder
members receive task.claimed with leaseUntil
an operation on the winning run, or a heartbeat from its computer, moves leaseUntil forward
with the daemon stopped, the claim is dropped 60 s after the last renewal and members receive task.updated with no claim
the claiming agent's owner releases the claim; the holding run's next operation on the task gets forbidden
each way a claim ends (expiry, release, run end, stop) sends members one claim.released with that cause

features.description: jm_post enforces the headline contract and the pod stamps the receipt
steps: a post without summary gets summary_required; one over 120 chars gets invalid_input
an ask without options, or a non-ask with needs, gets invalid_input
a post carrying receipt is rejected
a valid ask creates a message whose receipt has the runId, harness fake, wakeReason and toolCalls equal to the MCP calls made so far
the ask carries an open decision

features.description: A human rules on an ask once, and the agent is woken with the ruling and finishes the task
steps: a member sends decision.rule with an option id
members receive message.updated with the decision ruled and frozen
a second ruling returns already_ruled and changes nothing
the agent receives run.wake with reason decision_ruled
the agent calls jm_task_update done and members receive task.updated done

features.description: Tokens are scoped: a run cannot cross pods, an ended run is dead, and test routes are absent in production
steps: a jmr_ for pod A posting to pod B gets forbidden
after POST /v1/runs/:run/end the same jmr_ gets unauthorized
an actor field in MCP tool arguments is ignored
the production build of the Worker contains no /__test handler
a pod owner stops a live run; the daemon receives run.stop, the run ends cancelled, and its jmr_ gets unauthorized at once

features.description: The whole slice runs end to end with the fake agent in under 60 s
steps: sign in, create pod, invite, join
start the daemon and add the fake agent
create a task assigned to it
observe run.wake, task.claimed, then an ask with a receipt
rule on the ask, observe the second wake and task.updated done
E2E_MS under 60000

features.description: jellymoon login signs in with GitHub's device flow and stores a user token safely
steps: against a stub GitHub, jellymoon login prints the user code and verification URL
the person signs in through the server's GitHub OAuth web flow (the stub) and approves the code at POST /v1/auth/device/approve; POST /v1/auth/device/token then returns a jmu_ exactly once
the token file is mode 0600 and the token is never printed
a revoked or invalid GitHub token gets unauthorized

features.description: A recorded real Claude Code session (claude-agent-acp) replays through the daemon and makes the slice's pod calls
steps: daemon/testdata/acp/claude-slice.jsonl is recorded against the pinned adapter, scrubbed
the replay test drives the daemon with it and the pod calls match the golden list
one operator walks the slice by hand with real Claude Code and the result is noted in progress.md

features.description: Every PR boots the server as a self-hoster runs it, from the PR's own build, and the contract suite passes against it
steps: the e2e-deployed job builds the server bundle and boots it as its own process on a Postgres service container, with env config only (make deployed-boot)
deployed-boot refuses a server with no database, finds the test routes closed in the hosted shape, serves a pod through the real routes and keeps it across kill -9
the contract suite, TestF14Budget included, passes with that bundle as the server under test (make e2e-deployed); a server that fails to boot fails the job

features.description: A person uses the slice from the client chosen in the client options review
steps: the four slice screens (/device, /pod/:id, the needs-you queue as a filter on the same stream, /invite/:token) render inside one layout shell
/device approves a daemon's device code after GitHub sign-in
/pod/:id shows each card with its summary line, status and receipt chip, folded body and composer
the needs-you filter lists the open asks of the same stream, and a, 1..n and j/k work with the keyboard only
pressing a on an open ask makes the ruled state appear live over the WebSocket, with no reload
/invite/:token joins a teammate who has no install to the pod
the same specs pass at 390 and 1440 px, with no horizontal page scroll and no clipped text on any route
features.test: Playwright specs at 390 and 1440 px: sign-in and /device approval; open pod, see card, press a, ruled state appears live; invite link join; layout invariants on each route; keyboard approve driven by key presses, not clicks

features.description: An agent reads Linear through a pod grant without ever holding the Linear token
steps: against a stub Linear, a pod admin connects Linear and grants an agent read access through the pod
the agent reads Linear through the pod grant, and the result comes back to it
the Linear token is absent from every agent-visible payload: tool lists, results, errors and the run's env
a write call from the agent parks as a decision card with the exact arguments, and the stub Linear sees no write while it is parked
one approval releases exactly one upstream call; a rejection or expiry releases none
the receipt is stamped by the server and links the card, the approver and the result
features.test: go test ./e2e -run TestF19 (against a stub Linear)

features.description: A recorded real Codex session (codex-acp) replays through the daemon and makes the slice's pod calls
steps: daemon/testdata/acp/codex-slice.jsonl is recorded against the pinned adapter, scrubbed
the replay test passes

features.description: Evidence is served: the pod stamps every run operation as a tool-call record, and the evidence read returns them
steps: a run makes three MCP calls; its run token reads three tc_ records, source pod, in order, each with a digest, in the shape ToolCallRecord fixes
a member's user token reads the same records; a non-member, another run's token and another pod's token get forbidden
a toolCalls or actor field an agent sends is ignored, and no operation writes a record
the read returns at most 500 records, and the count matches the run receipt's toolCalls
features.test: go test ./e2e -run TestF21 (server; the Worker adds TestF21 to E2E_A_SKIP, docs/development/e2e-contract.md)

features.description: A pod owner connects a connector, grants it to an agent and names approvers from the CLI, not hand-built HTTP
steps: jellymoon connector connect reads the token from JELLYMOON_CONNECTOR_TOKEN or a hidden prompt, never argv, and the token is never printed, logged or written to the config dir
connector grant takes --access read or write-with-confirm, and --access write is refused client-side
connector approvers replaces the set and an empty list clears it
connector list shows pinned operations by access level and never a credential; connector receipts shows the server's receipts
a drift refusal prints connector_drift naming the operation; a non-owner gets forbidden and a non-zero exit
features.test: go test ./e2e -run TestF22 (server; against the stub Linear F19 uses; Worker skip listed in E2E_A_SKIP and docs/development/e2e-contract.md)

features.description: An ask whose claims cite nothing, or whose numbers are not in the cited call, is refused ungrounded
steps: an ask with a claim citing nothing gets 422 ungrounded
a cite of an id that is not a record in this pod, or a tool call from another agent's run, gets ungrounded
a number in a claim's text that is in neither the cited call's digest nor a cited message gets ungrounded
a fully cited ask is accepted and F11, F12 and F14 still pass
the refusal names the claim index and never echoes the digest
features.test: go test ./e2e -run TestF25 (server; the Worker adds TestF25 to E2E_A_SKIP, docs/development/e2e-contract.md)
